subject.title: fix: Responses streams mishandle interleaved output items and silent truncation

question: After the ChatGPT terminal-event defect is fixed, should the combined retry, storage, role, token-floor, and session-header behavior changes land together in this provider-runtime PR?
rationale: These changes alter several compatibility-sensitive provider defaults and contracts; tests can prove mechanics, but an owner must confirm the intended cross-provider upgrade policy and acceptable rollout scope.

options.title: Fix and prove combined change
options.body: Keep the cohesive stream-hardening PR, fix ChatGPT error finalization, refresh against main, and require focused OpenAI, Azure, and ChatGPT compatibility proof before merge.

options.title: Split compatibility changes
options.body: Land the per-index and terminal-state repair separately, then review retry, role, storage, token-floor, and header changes as narrower follow-up PRs.

options.title: Accept current scope
options.body: Merge the broad provider behavior changes after the terminal fix while explicitly accepting that some non-OpenAI paths have only mocked coverage.

recommendation.title: Fix and prove combined change
recommendation.body: Keep the cohesive stream-hardening PR, fix ChatGPT error finalization, refresh against main, and require focused OpenAI, Azure, and ChatGPT compatibility proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The provider transport adapter and surrounding Responses runtime history point to Vincent Koc as the strongest available owner for the cross-provider contract decision.
